content: Supra Player: Compare & Sync Videos Fast | Product Hunt Launching today Supra Player Launching today Compare & Sync Videos Fast 159 followers Compare & Sync Videos Fast 159 followers Visit website Supra Player is a lightweight macOS app built for reviewing, comparing, and syncing video. Compare up to 12 videos side by side with frame-accurate playback, automatic audio sync, shared zoom and pan, customizable layouts, annotations, and instant switching—without the complexity of a full video editor. Overview Reviews Alternatives Built with Team More Free Options Launch tags: Productivity • User Experience • Video Launch Team / Built With Show more Show more Launching Today # 7 Day Rank Upvote • 126 points Follow Supra Player Add to collection Share Analytics Company Info supraplayer.jessengatai.com App Store Supra Player Info Launched in 2026 Forum p/supra-player Similar Products Screen Studio Beautiful screen recordings in minutes 4.9 ( 177 reviews ) Product demo Screenshots and screen recording apps CapCut All-in-one video editing app for creating TikTok videos 4.3 ( 40 reviews ) Video editing Mobile editing apps Tella Screen recording for entrepreneurs 4.8 ( 36 reviews ) Screenshots and screen recording apps Video Compare A mac app to compare multiple videos side by side ツSupercut Blazing fast, AI Video Messaging for teams 5.0 ( 10 reviews ) View more Subscribe Sign in Social X Viktor.com The AI employee that does the work, in Slack & Teams Try Viktor.com Promoted What do you think? … Login to comment Jesse Ngatai Supra Player Maker 📌 Hey everyone! I'm Jesse, the maker of Supra Player. I'm a software developer, but I also enjoy editing videos as a hobby. Lately I've been spending a lot of time experimenting with AI video workflows—upscaling, frame interpolation, restoration, outpainting, and comparing outputs from different models. I kept finding myself opening heavyweight editors like Final Cut Pro just to review or compare videos, which felt like overkill. I wanted something that launched instantly, stayed lightweight, and focused purely on reviewing, comparing, and syncing footage—without timelines, project files, or the complexity of a full editor. Essentially, I wanted a video player built for analysis rather than editing. What started as a tool for my own workflow gradually became the video player I used more than QuickTime, so I decided to polish it up and release it. If you work with video—whether it's AI, multicam productions, podasts, VFX, content creation, or client reviews—I hope you find it useful. Thanks for checking it out, and I'm happy to answer any questions! summary: Compose music with just your voice
content: Nada: Compose music with just your voice | Product Hunt Launching today Nada Launching today Compose music with just your voice 289 followers Compose music with just your voice 289 followers Visit website Nada is the easiest way to turn your voice into music. Hum, sing, or whistle an idea, and instantly convert it into MIDI. Arrange your melodies on mobile, choose from a variety of instruments, and build songs wherever inspiration strikes. No AI generation involved, just your own creativity, captured faster. Overview Reviews Alternatives Built with Team Awards More Free Options Launch tags: Music • Audio • Electronic Music Launch Team / Built With Show more Show more Launching Today # 3 Day Rank Upvote • 225 points Follow Nada Add to collection Share Analytics Company Info go.tunelab.id/download Nada Info Launched in 2026 Forum p/nada-2 Similar Products Guitar Wiz All-in-one guitar companion app to learn, practice & create 5.0 ( 2 reviews ) Note and writing apps Search Kodai App Convert audio recordings to midi, organize and collaborate 5.0 ( 1 review ) Simpia Level up piano skill faster 4.7 ( 9 reviews ) Customer support tools AI Generative Media Soundverse AI AI Assistant for Music Creators 3.3 ( 3 reviews ) AI Generative Media AudioCipher Creative melody generator VST for music producers 5.0 ( 1 review ) View more Subscribe Sign in Social X Viktor.com The AI employee that does the work, in Slack & Teams Try Viktor.com Promoted What do you think? … Login to comment Bregas S. Wicaksono Nada Maker 📌 Last November, my friends and I started thinking about how we could make it easier for musicians to create music anywhere, anytime. At the time, we watched the making of video for Stromae’s “Alors on danse.” It was funny, but also inspiring. It made us wonder: what if people could create music using only their voice? A lot of people have great musical ideas, but they cannot always play an instrument. Traditional DAWs can also feel too complex, especially when all you want to do is capture an idea quickly. But almost everyone can hum, sing, or whistle a melody. That was the moment everything clicked. We decided to build Nada, which means “tune” in Indonesian. At first, we imagined it as a better voice notes app for musicians, something simple for capturing musical ideas. But as we kept building, it slowly became a mini DAW: voice-to-MIDI, instruments, arrangement, beats, and music production features, all designed to stay simple and not overwhelming. Today, we’re excited and proud to finally share Nada on Product Hunt. We built Nada for musicians, creators, and anyone who has ever had a melody in their head but struggled to turn it into music. We’d love to hear your feedback, ideas, and thoughts. And if you’re a musician, creator, investor, partner, or someone who believes music creation should be more accessible, we’d love to connect. For more inquiries, you can contact us via email: tunelabid@gmail.com Thank you for checking out Nada! Upvote (8) Repo

Every QA team knows what they want to test. "Log in, add an item to the cart, check the order confirmation." Saying it takes ten seconds. Then the team spends six months turning that sentence into something a machine will run: step definitions, selectors, automation glue, flaky scripts that break on every UI change. The intent was never the hard part. The execution layer was the tax. CoWork takes your existing natural-language or BDD test cases, converts them into structured BDD/Gherkin context, builds an execution plan, and runs the test on a real mobile device. When the app behaves differently, like a changed label, unexpected popup, or interrupted flow, CoWork replans and asks for human approval before moving ahead. When it needs input, like an OTP, it pauses instead of guessing. If it can’t proceed, it fails honestly instead of faking a pass. Who it’s for: QA leaders, SDETs, mobile engineering teams, and product teams with existing test cases but low execution coverage before releases. Common use cases: Regression testing, Release readiness, checkout/login flows, OTP-heavy journeys, app flows that break often, and teams trying to reduce manual execution without rewriting everything from scratch. What makes CoWork different is the balance: AI execution where it can move fast, human control where judgment matters. If you run mobile tests, I’d genuinely love your take. Try it here: ht
